newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FOREIGN FUND INFLOW KEEPS HUNGARY O/N RATES LOW.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGN FUND INFLOW KEEPS HUNGARY O/N RATES LOW.

text.p: Hungary's overnight interest rates were steady throughout the week as abundant money supply prevailed due to the inflow of foreign funds, dealers said.
On Friday, overnight rates traded between 19.625 and 19.875 percent with most deals struck at 19.75 percent, and finished at 19.625 percent, unchanged from Thursday.
Traders said the abundant money supply was probably due to the inflow of foreign funds moving over from countries such as the Czech Republic and Poland.
"While it is true that a significant part of that money goes to the bourse, it does come through the banks," said Sandor Tolonics of Commerzbank.

The Budapest Stock Exchange is regarded as somewhat of a safe heaven among European emerging markets, mainly due to improving fundamentals of Hungary as well as floods and financial uncertainties in other east European countries.
